Tuesday 17 November 2026 · 24 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.58% to 25,291 but decliners led 1,861 to 710
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned -0.51% weighted by turnover, against -1.20% for the median stock, a gap of 0.7 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

TVS Supply Chain Solutions Limited rose 12.2% on 75 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

VIP Clothing Limited rose 1.3% on 65 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “VIP Clothing Limited has submitted to the Exchange, the financial results for the period ended September 30, 2026.”.

Yatra Online Limited rose 20.0% on 64 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

The exchange has formally asked 1 company to explain today's move: RPSG VENTURES LIMITED. Those queries were filed after the close, so they confirm the move rather than explain it. NSE's own surveillance flagged the same names.

Coal India unit Mahanadi seeks $9.6 billion valuation in IPO
Coal India subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields plans an initial public offering targeting a $9.6 billion valuation. The listing establishes a market benchmark for Coal India’s highest-margin subsidiary, which generates nearly half of its consolidated profit. Parent-level capital unlocking could narrow Coal India's holding company valuation discount once draft red herring prospectus filings confirm the issue structure.
Reuters Business · +2 others
Rupee rises, volatility ebbs as equity inflows blunt global headwinds
Strong foreign portfolio equity inflows drove the Indian rupee higher while currency volatility indicators dropped to multi-week lows. Sustained currency stability lowers landed input costs for domestic manufacturers and oil refiners, though it caps net rupee realizations for IT and pharma exporters. Weekly net foreign portfolio investment data will confirm whether domestic liquidity can continue insulating local valuations from elevated global interest rates.

Connected to your data
AI disruption wipes out $206 billion in market value of 10 listed companies; which businesses are most at risk?
Generative AI tools erased $206 billion in market capitalization across ten global software, education, and marketplace companies since 2021 despite revenue expansion. The selloff highlights structural margin risks for businesses whose core workflows face automated substitution. For Indian IT services and internet platforms, this threatens long-term pricing power and valuation multiples. Global software contract renewal rates will indicate how rapidly pricing power decays.
Mint Markets
TVS Supply Chain Solutions shares jump 17% after Q2 results, surge 24% in 2 weeks; what lies ahead? Key levels to watch
TVS Supply Chain Solutions reported Q2 revenue growth of 38% year on year to ₹3,687.2 crore, while net profit doubled to ₹36.5 crore. The operational outperformance demonstrates operating leverage within third-party logistics, driving margin expansion across contract management segments. Sustained contract wins in global forwarding will confirm whether the company can maintain high revenue growth through the remaining fiscal year.

Global Market Today: Asian stocks fall as Wall Street selloff deepens ahead of Nvidia earnings
Asian equity benchmarks fell after a selloff in US technology stocks pulled the Nasdaq down 2.7% ahead of Nvidia earnings. Global tech volatility reaches India by triggering foreign portfolio capital outflows and pressuring IT exporters reliant on US enterprise technology budgets. Foreign institutional investor daily cash market flow figures will confirm whether global risk aversion causes net equity selling in India.

Asia shares stumble on tech weakness ahead of Nvidia earnings
Asian equity benchmarks declined up to 1.5% as tech stocks sold off ahead of Nvidia's quarterly earnings announcement. The global tech pull-back depresses valuation multiples across Nifty IT constituents, while foreign institutional investors trim emerging market risk exposure. Nvidia's forward revenue guidance on Wednesday night will determine whether global fund flows resume towards technology services exporters like Infosys and TCS.

US enterprise clients cutting software budgets to fund AI infrastructure reduces order inflows for Indian IT service companies, pressuring dollar-denominated revenue growth. US tech enterprise software spending data in upcoming quarterly filings will confirm if discretionary tech budgets are shrinking further.

Vikram Solar vs Premier vs Waaree vs Suzlon: Green energy stocks under pressure - What do technical charts signal?
Solar module manufacturers Waaree Energies and Premier Energies fell alongside Suzlon Energy as high valuation multiples faced selling pressure. Declining domestic solar module prices compress gross margins for equipment manufacturers, while simultaneously lowering capital expenditure costs for power producers like NTPC Green and Adani Green. Blended average selling price metrics in upcoming quarterly operational updates will indicate the extent of margin compression.

India's markets regulator forms panel to simplify capital-raising rules
SEBI established an expert panel to review and simplify capital-raising regulations for listed companies, focusing on preferential issues and rights offers. Faster execution timelines and reduced compliance costs will lower the cost of capital for expanding firms. Financial sector intermediaries and highly leveraged corporate issuers stand to gain from streamlined equity dilution processes.

Sensex, Nifty gain over 0.5% as banks, FMCG shine; broader market slips
Large-cap indices gained 0.5% on strength in banking and FMCG, while the SmallCap 250 fell 0.96% and the Healthcare index rose 3.57%. Institutional flows shifted toward defensive earnings and reasonable bank valuations, abandoning stretched small-cap multiples. Sustained small-cap earnings delivery in upcoming quarterly filings will test whether this valuation correction spreads further.

Macro and economy
RBA board judges fifth rate hike needed to provide policy assurance
The Reserve Bank of Australia signaled a fifth interest rate hike to anchor inflation expectations. Direct transmission to Indian equities is minimal, though sustained global central bank tightening maintains upward pressure on yield differentials and keeps foreign portfolio flows selective across emerging markets. Monthly FPI equity inflow trends will confirm if risk appetite remains muted.

Sebi may propose raising FPI beneficial ownership threshold to 25%; plans consultation paper
SEBI plans to issue a consultation paper proposing to raise the ultimate beneficial ownership threshold for foreign portfolio investors from 10% to 25%. The change aligns Indian regulations with global standards and reduces administrative burdens for foreign funds. Eased compliance requirements lower barrier costs for overseas allocations, supporting institutional liquidity across high-market-cap Indian equities.

India raises diesel, jet fuel export levies as inflation stays elevated
The government increased export duties on diesel and aviation turbine fuel to curb domestic inflation and capture excess refining margins. Higher levies reduce net realized refining margins for private and public refiners, notably impacting Reliance Industries' standalone earnings. Upcoming fortnightly windfall tax revisions will indicate how long refining profitability remains capped.
Reuters Business
India raises export duty on diesel and aviation turbine fuel
India increased export duties on diesel and jet fuel to contain domestic price pressures after wholesale inflation reached 12.3%. The duty hike reduces gross refining margins for downstream exporters like Reliance Industries while capping domestic freight costs for manufacturing and logistics companies. Next week's retail inflation print will show whether fiscal intervention successfully moderates headline price indices.

China’s Buyback Push Struggles to Put a Floor Under Stocks
Chinese listed companies have drawn down less than 10% of Beijing's 300-billion-yuan special re-lending facility for stock buybacks. Persistent weakness in Chinese equities prevents sustained foreign capital rotation out of India into cheap Chinese valuations. Furthermore, soft Chinese domestic demand keeps global industrial commodity prices low, supporting operating margins for Indian manufacturing and infrastructure firms.

PB Balaji drove Tata Motors out of debt. JLR is dragging it back in
Tata Motors faces renewed balance sheet pressure after its British unit, Jaguar Land Rover, reported a negative free cash flow of £484 million in the second quarter. JLR generates over 70% of consolidated revenue, so operating deleverage there directly squeezes group EBIT margins. This cash burn halts the parent company's deleveraging trajectory and risks valuation downgrades across Indian auto tickers.
Mint Companies
Wall Street update: Why Walmart, Home Depot, Target, Lowe's stocks are in focus this week | Q3 earnings latest news
Major US retailers including Walmart and Target report Q3 earnings this week, providing a direct gauge of US consumer discretionary spending. Soft sales or margin compression in these results signals weakening order books for Indian home textile exporters and apparel manufacturers. Additionally, reduced retail tech spending threatens discretionary order inflows for tier-one Indian IT service exporters.
Mint Markets
Geopolitics
Warsh Says Fed Is Gaming Out How AI Could Reshape Economy - WSJ
Former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh noted that the Federal Reserve is modeling how artificial intelligence adoption could increase long-term productivity and reduce structural inflation. If productivity gains keep US potential GDP growth high, US interest rates may remain elevated for longer. That outcome would keep the US dollar strong, narrowing the India-US rate differential and weighing on foreign fund flows.
Fed and rates
India's 2025-26 edible oil import bill up 24 pc to record Rs 2 lakh cr; crude palm oil buying surges
India's edible oil import bill climbed 24% to a record Rs 2 lakh crore, driven by a surge in crude palm oil shipments. The expanding bill widens India's trade deficit, pressuring the rupee. Elevated palm oil costs raise input inflation for FMCG firms like Hindustan Unilever, while domestic processors like Adani Wilmar benefit from higher realizations.
